| Category = Seafood recipes
| Difficulty = 3
}}

{{recipe}}

This '''pouch-roasted snapper''' cooks perfectly in 30 minutes.

== Ingredients ==
* 2 [[Cookbook:Cup|cups]] quick-cook [[Cookbook:Couscous|couscous]]
* 1 whole (2 [[Cookbook:Pound|lb]]/1 [[Cookbook:Kilogram|kg]]) [[Cookbook:Red Snapper|red snapper]], cleaned, fins removed, head and tail intact
* [[Cookbook:Salt|Salt]]
* Freshly ground [[Cookbook:Pepper|black pepper]]
* ½ large bunch each of [[Cookbook:Dill|dill]], [[Cookbook:Oregano|oregano]], [[Cookbook:Thyme|thyme]], and [[Cookbook:Parsley|parsley]]
* 1 ½ sprigs [[Cookbook:Rosemary|rosemary]]
* 2 large [[Cookbook:Lemon|lemons]], thinly [[Cookbook:Slicing|sliced]]
* 2 [[Cookbook:Tablespoon|tbsp]] [[Cookbook:Worcestershire Sauce|Worcestershire sauce]]
* ½ cup dry white [[Cookbook:Wine|wine]]
* ¼ cup [[Cookbook:Butter|butter]], cut into small cubes

== Procedure ==
#Rinse the couscous, then sprinkle with kosher salt and allow to sit for 10 minutes.
#Lay the fish diagonally on a [[Cookbook:Parchment Paper|parchment]]-lined [[Cookbook:Baking Pan|baking pan]]. Sprinkle liberally with salt and black pepper, inside and out. Stuff with the herbs and several slices of lemon. Place remaining lemon slices under fish.
#Run couscous through a [[Cookbook:Sieve|sieve]] all around the fish. Drizzle Worcestershire sauce and white white over fish. Dollop butter all over top.
#Top with another piece of parchment and staple shut.
#[[Cookbook:Baking|Bake]] at 425°F (about 215°C) for 30 minutes. Open with a paring knife and serve.
